title: Move envelope speed measurement
goal: Measure move envelope proof performance end to end, establish a baseline, implement only evidence-backed speed improvements, and prove the changes make future envelope validation faster without weakening target-native support or fail-closed refusal behavior.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove a repeatable baseline measurement exists for representative move envelope proof chunks, including boot time, provisioning time, per-proof duration, coverage verification time, and total wall time.
proofChecklist.evidence: Repeatable baseline measured with scripts/smoke/move-envelope-speed-plan.json and scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs in fresh mode. Command: node scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs --plan scripts/smoke/move-envelope-speed-plan.json --out-dir /tmp/move-envelope-speed-baseline-fresh --mode fresh --label baseline-fresh --json. Result passed in totalWallMs=123232 (shell elapsed 123.266s). Artifacts retained under /tmp/move-envelope-speed-baseline-fresh. Chunk timings: file-identity-pilot wallMs=43082 with boot-pair 340ms, provision skipped 15ms, stat-file 10685ms, unsafe-stat-refusal 31464ms; listener-refusal-pilot wallMs=79995 with boot-pair 287ms, provision skipped 16ms, socat-file-responder 18725ms, unsafe-socat-file-responder-refusal 60377ms. Coverage verification wallMs=155, expectedCount=4, coveredCount=4, missing=[], failed=[].

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the baseline measurements identify the slowest phases and classify them by cause, such as VM boot, broad apt provisioning, row-local package install, guest exec overhead, service readiness wait, compression/archive fixture setup, or remote transport overhead.
proofChecklist.evidence: Baseline bottleneck classification: slowest phases are proof/refusal work, not boot or provisioning, because this representative plan uses skipProvision. Per-proof durations: unsafe-socat-file-responder-refusal 60377ms (dominant listener refusal path with active-client, unsupported-shape, changed-file, port-conflict, and missing-binary checks), unsafe-stat-refusal 31464ms (changed file and unsupported stat/symlink refusals), socat-file-responder 18725ms (service start/readiness and target response), stat-file 10685ms. VM boot was only 627ms total across fresh chunks; provisioning was skipped and cost 31ms. Coverage verification cost 155ms. This identifies parallel chunk execution as the meaningful wall-time optimization for this plan; warm VM reuse can only save the tiny boot/provision slice.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove a benchmark harness or script can run the same chunk plan before and after changes, retain JSON/timing artifacts, compute comparable totals, and print a concise speed report.
proofChecklist.evidence: Added benchmark/report harnesses: scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs runs a chunk plan in fresh, warm, or parallel mode, retains per-chunk JSON/timing artifacts and benchmark-summary.json, runs coverage verification, and preserves failure classification; scripts/move-envelope-speed-report.mjs compares before/after summary dirs and prints total, matrix timing, coverage, and per-chunk percent changes. Syntax checks passed with node --check for both scripts. Reports generated successfully: warm report from /tmp/move-envelope-speed-baseline-fresh to /tmp/move-envelope-speed-after-warm and parallel report from /tmp/move-envelope-speed-baseline-fresh to /tmp/move-envelope-speed-after-parallel.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove at least one safe speed improvement is implemented and measured, such as warm-VM reuse for compatible chunks, smarter proof provisioning, reduced guest exec calls, parallel chunk execution, or cached proof overlays, without hiding semantic proof failures.
proofChecklist.evidence: Implemented and measured safe parallel chunk execution in scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs with --mode parallel. It runs independent chunk-plan chunks concurrently in separate fresh VM pairs and does not retry or suppress semantic failures. Parallel command passed: node scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs --plan scripts/smoke/move-envelope-speed-plan.json --out-dir /tmp/move-envelope-speed-after-parallel --mode parallel --label after-parallel --json. Result totalWallMs=80223 (shell elapsed 80.250s), both chunks passed, and coverage passed 4/4. Warm-VM reuse was also measured but only improved total from 123.232s to 122.426s (-0.7%), proving boot/provision was not the useful target for this plan.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the speed improvement is real by comparing before/after measurements on the same representative chunk plan and recording percent change for total time and the affected phase.
proofChecklist.evidence: Before/after speed report proves a real wall-time improvement on the same plan. Baseline fresh total 123.232s; after parallel total 80.223s; delta -34.9%. Matrix timings stayed effectively identical (121.909s -> 122.042s, +0.1%), showing correctness work was not skipped; it was overlapped across independent chunks. Coverage remained effectively identical (0.155s -> 0.162s). Per-chunk wall/timing remained stable: file-identity-pilot 43.082s -> 43.215s wall, listener-refusal-pilot 79.995s -> 80.060s wall. Speedup comes from parallelizing independent chunks, not weakening proof work.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove support/refusal correctness is preserved after speed changes: every expected proof in the benchmark plan still passes with visible target evidence for support rows and no target pid or no loader launch for gatekeeper rows.
proofChecklist.evidence: Correctness preserved after speed changes. Parallel benchmark coverage passed with expectedCount=4, coveredCount=4, missing=[], failed=[]. Support evidence remained present: stat-file recorded targetOutputFirstLine="  File: /tmp/stat-file.txt", targetSize=12, matching targetSha; socat-file-responder recorded response="hello-socat-file" and targetPid. Gatekeeper evidence remained present: unsafe-stat-refusal recorded changedFileLoaderState=refused and changedFileTargetPid=null; unsafe-socat-file-responder-refusal recorded active/unsupported state omission plus changedFileTargetPid=null, portConflictTargetPid=null, and missingSocatTargetPid=null.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove infrastructure failures remain separated from semantic failures and any retry or parallelization logic retries only classified infrastructure failures, never assertion failures or envelope refusals that indicate a real bug.
proofChecklist.evidence: Infrastructure and semantic failures remain separated. The benchmark harness keeps per-chunk stdout/stderr and records parsed matrix failure objects when present; otherwise it applies the same conservative infrastructure classifier regex used by scripts/move-envelope-failure-classifier.mjs. Parallel mode does not retry anything, so semantic failures cannot be retried away. Existing classifier proof from the framework work remains applicable: synthetic EXEC_AGENT_TIMEOUT/VsockExec logs classify as infrastructure, while AssertionError/changed-file-identity/targetPid-null logs classify as semantic.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove remote amd64 speed measurement is either supported by the same harness or explicitly documented as not run with a reason and a follow-up next action; do not claim remote speedup without remote timing evidence.
proofChecklist.evidence: Remote amd64 speed measurement was not run in this goal, and no remote speedup is claimed. Reason: this goal first established a local repeatable benchmark and proved a local parallel chunk speedup; running the same timing benchmark remotely would consume additional remote VM time and should be a follow-up once the local harness is accepted. Follow-up next action: run node scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs with --mode fresh and --mode parallel on root@192.168.0.8 using the existing Linux MACHINEN_VMM/MACHINEN_GVPROXY remote setup, then compare with scripts/move-envelope-speed-report.mjs. Remote support is partially prepared by the earlier remote wrapper pattern, but this evidence row intentionally does not claim remote timing improvement.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove local static and unit validation passes after speed-harness or matrix changes, including format, lint, docs/API if public exports changed, typecheck, smoke manifest check if scripts changed, focused move tests, and fallow audit.
proofChecklist.evidence: Final local validation passed after speed benchmark/harness changes. Commands/timings: pnpm run format:check passed in 1.220s after formatting scripts/move-envelope-speed-benchmark.mjs and scripts/move-envelope-speed-report.mjs with oxfmt 0.241s; pnpm run lint passed in 0.572s; pnpm run build:docs passed in 1.894s; pnpm run typecheck passed in 2.877s including full pnpm build; pnpm run check-smoke-manifest passed in 0.142s with 70 entries; focused Vitest passed 4 files / 213 tests in 0.920s; pnpm exec fallow audit --changed-since origin/main passed in 0.571s with no issues across 59 changed files.

doneWhen: All required proofChecklist rows have status proven with evidence, and no stop condition applies.

verification.proves: Representative move envelope chunks still emit usable per-phase and per-proof timings.
Before/after timing artifacts are comparable and produce a percent-change speed report.
Every expected proof in the benchmark plan passed and no expected row is missing.
Formatting remains valid after benchmark or matrix changes.
Lint and health guard remain valid after benchmark or matrix changes.
TypeScript remains valid after benchmark or matrix changes.
Smoke/proof script manifest remains valid if scripts are added or changed.
Focused move behavior tests still pass.
Architecture and health audit passes for changed code.

stopIf: A proposed optimization would weaken target-native envelope evidence, skip required support/refusal checks, or hide semantic failures as infrastructure flakes.
A proposed optimization requires proof-only tools to be baked into base assets instead of proof VMs or disposable overlays.
Measurements are too noisy or incomplete to support a speedup claim, and no stable benchmark plan can be produced.
Required local VMM assets or remote access are unavailable for the measurement scope being claimed.
A required validation command fails and cannot be fixed within the current goal scope.
The /goal loop reaches 8 agent completion(s) without satisfying the contract.
